name: AUM Namah Shivaya
meaning: I bow to Shiva, the auspicious and transformative presence.
purpose: A short devotional invocation for beginning meditation and returning attention to steadiness.
supports: Pausing before reacting; patience; present-moment awareness; inner composure.
when: At the beginning of meditation, during quiet reflection, or whenever a simple anchor is helpful.
note: A widely used nama mantra, the Panchakshara (“five syllables”). Its place on Monday reflects the common Shiva–Somavara association; it is not restricted to Mondays.
source: The Panchakshara of the Sri Rudram (Krishna Yajurveda)
